<div class="proj-detail-body">
  <div class="proj-detail-prose-wrap">

    <h2 class="proj-detail-h2">About the project</h2>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">Weird Worlds is an education and outreach initiative that uses OpenSpace to make astrobiology &mdash; the study of life's potential beyond Earth &mdash; accessible to diverse audiences. Kaz Gary, a PhD student at The Ohio State University studying exoplanets, focuses his research on identifying where to look for life and what biosignatures might betray its presence. This 2025 SCoPE Seed Grant project, supported through Arizona State University, translates that research into planetarium shows and social media content designed for classrooms, museums, and community spaces.</p>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">The project explores concepts like planetary habitability, biosignatures, and the criteria that make a world friendly to life &mdash; using OpenSpace's visualization capabilities to let audiences actually see the candidate worlds and systems being discussed. Gary also writes for Astrobites, a graduate-student-run astronomy blog, and brings experience presenting live planetarium shows to public audiences.</p>

    <div class="proj-facts-row">
      <span class="proj-fact">NASA Astrophysics Division</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Exoplanet astrobiology</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Planetary habitability</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Biosignatures</span>
      <span class="proj-fact">Planetarium show development</span>
    </div>

    <h2 class="proj-detail-h2">How OpenSpace is used</h2>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">Gary develops new exoplanet content within OpenSpace specifically for this project &mdash; visualizations of candidate habitable worlds and the stellar systems that host them. A comprehensive program guide for live planetarium presentations is a core deliverable, one that will benefit not only this project's local audiences but the broader OpenSpace user community once released.</p>
    <p class="proj-detail-p">Social media videos based on OpenSpace visuals accompany the planetarium program, extending the project's reach to online audiences who may never visit a dome in person.</p>

    <div class="proj-quote">
      <p class="proj-quote-text">"Developing planetarium shows is one of the most awe-inspiring ways to communicate science, and with OpenSpace, I'll be able to bring cutting-edge astronomy directly to the public in a way that's both accurate and visually stunning."</p>
      <p class="proj-quote-attribution">Kaz Gary &middot; PhD Student, The Ohio State University</p>
    </div>

    <div class="proj-quote">
      <p class="proj-quote-text">"Kaz's plans to develop a program guide for a live planetarium program using the new exoplanet assets he produces in OpenSpace supports the needs of our OpenSpace project by providing program resources for other users."</p>
      <p class="proj-quote-attribution">Rosamond Kinzler, PhD &middot; OpenSpace PI, AMNH</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
